title: Generative retrieval for next-item recommendation
speaker: พัสกร ยืนยง
bullets: Encode product content as Semantic IDs
Learn to generate the next item ID from a user history
One real-data CPU experiment; two simple baselines
notes: Open with the task: given past events, predict the next product. The content encoder is pretrained; the recommendation Transformer starts from random weights. This is a teaching implementation with disclosed computational adaptations.

title: Data and chronological holdout
speaker: พัสกร ยืนยง
bullets: Amazon Beauty 2014: 2,000 users and 7,154 items
17,264 events → 13,264 train events → 11,264 examples
[A,B,C] train; D validation; E test
Test history includes D; training targets exclude D and E
notes: Explain metadata cleanup and the minimum five retained events per user. Each first training event has no nonempty prefix, giving 13,264 minus 2,000 training examples. All catalog metadata is available for ID learning, including held-out products. This is per-user chronology rather than a global temporal split.

title: From product content to unique Semantic IDs
speaker: พัสกร ยืนยง
bullets: Title, brand, category, price → Sentence-T5 vector [768]
Three residual codebooks: 256 vectors each
Append collision suffix; freeze 7,154 unique IDs
notes: At each level choose the nearest code vector, subtract it, and quantize the residual. Decode the sum to reconstruct the embedding. Reconstruction, codebook, and commitment losses train different paths. Three codes are learned; the fourth disambiguates collisions. The initial quantizer collapsed; warm-up and a lower learning rate restored usable codes, but quantized fine-tuning did not improve initialized reconstruction. Handoff: these fixed maps define the next presenter’s tokens.

title: Constructing model inputs and labels
speaker: ภาณุพงศ์ จันทร์ลาม
bullets: Input: user bucket + latest 20 item IDs + EOS
Input length ≤82; target length =5; vocabulary =3,026
PAD=0; EOS=1; ignored label padding =−100
notes: Offsets [2,258,514,770] distinguish code positions. User tokens use SHA-256 modulo 2,000 and can collide. The collator creates an attention mask. Walk through one example; distinguish integer ID tokens from the earlier continuous content embeddings.

title: Training and selecting the recommender
speaker: ภาณุพงศ์ จันทร์ลาม
bullets: Small T5 trained from scratch with teacher forcing
Labels [c0,c1,c2,c3,EOS]; input [PAD,c0,c1,c2,c3]
AdamW and mean token cross-entropy; 5,000 steps
Validation NDCG@10 selects step 4,500
notes: The encoder attends to observed history. Decoder causal attention prevents access to later target tokens; cross-attention uses the encoded history. At inference previous generated tokens replace true prefixes. Select every 500 steps on a fixed 500-user validation subset. Freeze before final test. best/ is inference; latest.pt additionally stores optimizer, RNG, and batching state for recovery.

title: Disclosed changes from the paper
speaker: ภาณุพงศ์ จันทร์ลาม
bullets: Encoder/decoder: 4+4 → 2+2 layers; heads: 6×64 → 4×32
Feed-forward: 1,024 → 512; batch: 256 → 64
Beauty training: 200,000 → 5,000 steps; smaller subset
Quantizer: Adam + warm-up; retrieval: catalog prefix constraints
notes: Paper RQ training uses Adagrad 0.4, batch 1,024, 20,000 epochs. Ours uses Adam 0.0001, CPU batch 16, ten warm-up plus seven completed quantized epochs. Recommender learning rate changes from 0.01 then inverse-square-root decay to constant 0.001. Quantizer selection uses reconstruction and recommender selection uses validation ranking. Explain practical compute and stability reasons, without claiming identical paper reproduction.

title: Generating and ranking catalog items
speaker: ธิปก ปัญญาวุธ
bullets: Beam width 20; generate four ID tokens and EOS
Trie permits catalog-valid continuations
Rank by summed token log-probabilities; return ten unique items
Generated tokens → raw SID → product lookup
notes: The target is never an argument to recommend. Strip the decoder start token before lookup. Constraints ensure validity, not relevance. Beam search is approximate. A narrow beam can discard a prefix leading to a stronger complete item. The saved trace generates an Olay cleansing system while the held-out target is Pureology shampoo; describe that mismatch honestly.

title: Two baselines and held-out results
speaker: ธิปก ปัญญาวุธ
bullets: Popularity: Recall@10 0.75%; NDCG@10 0.00279747
Item cosine: Recall@10 1.75%; NDCG@10 0.00655030
Top-ten hits: 15 / 35 / 47 out of 2,000 users
notes: Popularity counts original training events. Item cosine uses binary training-user co-occurrence, then sums similarities to observed history; ties use popularity and item ID. Both use the full catalog and allow repeated items. Recall is one held-out target hit; NDCG discounts its rank. Item cosine has no tuned hyperparameters. TIGER metrics are copied from the frozen original report, not rerun.

title: What the results support and leave open
speaker: ธิปก ปัญญาวุธ
bullets: Pipeline verified; TIGER exceeds two simple baselines in this run
Absolute accuracy remains low: 1,953 top-ten misses
One seed; no random-ID ablation or significance test
36.4% of test targets lack training events; subgroup accuracy unknown
notes: No causal claim that semantic structure produces the gain. All selected-catalog metadata is available, so do not claim an unseen-inventory cold-start evaluation. Full result-list coverage is not catalog diversity. Future work: matched random-ID ablation, stronger sequential baselines, repeated seeds, and training-seen/unseen subgroup analysis. Tests establish mechanics; ranking metrics establish this run’s quality.

title: Backup: quantization and gradient routing
speaker: พัสกร ยืนยง
bullets: c = argmin ||residual − codebook[j]||²
Residual subtracts the selected vector at each level
Forward: z + (quantized − z).detach() equals quantized
Backward: reconstruction reaches encoder; auxiliary losses train codebooks
notes: The argmin is discrete. Straight-through supplies a surrogate identity gradient to the encoder. Codebook loss detaches residuals; commitment loss detaches code vectors. Later residual losses detach earlier selected vectors. Reconstruction alone does not train codebooks through this path. Use test_straight_through_and_auxiliary_gradient_routing as evidence.

title: Backup: attention and tensor shapes
speaker: ภาณุพงศ์ จันทร์ลาม
bullets: Input IDs and attention mask: [batch,L], L≤82
Labels: [batch,5]; logits: [batch,5,3026]
Encoder self-attention uses observed history
Decoder: causal self-attention plus encoder cross-attention
notes: Explain Q, K and V as learned projections, with attention weights combining values based on query/key compatibility. The history is already observed, so encoder self-attention can use all its nonpadding positions. Decoder masking limits access to its prefix. Padding masks and causal masks have different jobs. T5 is supplied by Hugging Face; project code configures it and constructs the inputs.

title: Backup: baseline worked example
speaker: ธิปก ปัญญาวุธ
bullets: Training users: U1={a,b}; U2={a,c}
n(a)=2; n(b)=1; shared(a,b)=1
sim(a,b)=1/√2; sim(b,c)=0
Scores sum similarities; zero-score ties use training popularity
notes: Repeated events do not multiply binary co-occurrence counts. Self-similarity is zero. Test-time validation history is allowed as observed input, but the matrix is fitted only from train_items. Explain unseen items and empty-history fallback. All candidates remain eligible; no sampled negatives.

title: Backup: ranking scores and evaluation
speaker: ธิปก ปัญญาวุธ
bullets: Beam score = Σ log P(token | history, prefix)
Constraint masking does not prove globally optimal top K
Target at rank 3: Recall@5=1; NDCG@5=0.5
Empty predictions remain in averages; duplicates removed
notes: Full vocabulary probabilities underpin beam scores, rather than renormalizing over allowed trie tokens. The fixture test checks beam scores against exact item scoring with sufficiently wide beams. Distinguish full-catalog candidate eligibility from exhaustively scoring every item. coverage@10 means ten unique returned items per user.

title: Backup: frozen checkpoints and recovery
speaker: ภาณุพงศ์ จันทร์ลาม
bullets: best/ stores validation-selected inference weights
latest.pt stores model, optimizer, RNG, epoch, and batch cursor
Mapping and input hashes guard against incompatible restores
59 tests pass; original experiment recorded 57
notes: Dropout and shuffling require restored RNG state for exact continuation. Optimizer moments affect the next update. Restoring weights alone is insufficient. Exact resume is tested in the CPU environment, not promised across arbitrary systems. Use saved outputs if the conference demo cannot load dependencies.
